clue.text: It means raising the subject at the palace

definitions.text: It means raising the subject at the palace

parts.words: It means raising the subject at the palace
parts.note: a royal touch of the sword on the shoulder raises a loyal subject to knighthood at Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: Someone explains what a ceremony at court is for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising the subject' sounds like bringing up a topic in conversation; here it is promotion of a British subject to a knighthood at an investiture.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial tap of a sword that confers knighthood is the original meaning of this word for an honour.

clue.text: Inga wavering: accepting award or declining?

indicators.note: accepting means the shuffled name takes the prize inside itself
something wavering moves unsteadily, so the four letters of the name are shuffled

parts.note: a trophy is an award such as a cup

explanation.surface: Inga hesitates over whether her prize is a win or a sign of decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavering' turns INGA into AING, which, 'accepting' TROPHY, gives A + TROPHY + ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away or weakening is a gradual decline, as an unused muscle does.

parts.note: not rock and roll's ancestor, but a tune sung to a baby while rocking it to sleep, heard in earliest childhood

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a forerunner of rock music; the 'rock' is the gentle rocking of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby sung while rocking a baby is music from the very start of life, accompanying a rocking motion.

indicators.note: before puts the abbreviation ahead of the recess in the answer

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: Leaving before the break turns out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: An APSE is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or momentary error in judgement or memory is a minor mistake.

indicators.note: doing something without discrimination means in no particular order, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone flicks carelessly through an issue of the old humour magazine Punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a famous British humour magazine, which is where the surface points; the Suffolk Punch is also a breed of heavy farm horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy working horse used for pulling ploughs and carts, an example of the type.

clue.text: Look for quiet in a religious order

indicators.note: in places the quiet letter inside the group's name

parts.note: a sect is a religious group or denomination
P is the musical notation piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: Someone seeks peace and silence by joining a monastic community.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something, as in a building of gloomy aspect.

parts.note: short means little in height or length
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A complaint that office skills are not much use.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking dictation in a rapid system of abbreviated symbols was a core skill of a secretary.

definitions.meaning: the last parts or extremities of something

explanation.surface: Aspirations for the deciding matches of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both purposes one aims at and the concluding parts of anything.

clue.text: A wrong to right in short order

parts.note: right, put in short form, is abbreviated RT

explanation.surface: A grievance to be put right quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short order' usually means quickly; here it says right is shortened to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a civil wrong causing harm, for which damages may be claimed, is a tort.

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An invitation to return for the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up once more is to return or come back into view.

clue.text: Road in centre of South African frontier

indicators.note: in centre of places the road abbreviation in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent

explanation.surface: A highway running through the middle of a South African border region.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the line between two countries, the same thing as a frontier.

clue.text: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out

definitions.text: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out

parts.words: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out
parts.note: in cricket, a batsman who steps out of his crease can be stumped by the fielder behind the stumps knocking off the bails

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lawyer or friend helping someone in trouble; in cricket, removing the bails while the batsman's foot is out of the crease gets him out (stumped).
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder behind the stumps in cricket dismisses an advancing batsman by knocking the bails off.

clue.text: Let priest go to cast out unwanted spirit

indicators.note: to cast is to shape metal anew, and out signals a disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to let a priest perform an exorcism of a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's exorcism imagery makes 'cast out' look like part of the definition; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy, mischievous ghost that throws objects about is a spirit nobody wants in the house.

clue.text: Takes the car, beetles off and whoops it up

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of car and beetles are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drives a VW Beetle off and has a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: A Beetle is also a Volkswagen car, which feeds the driving picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To whoop it up is to party noisily, the same as marking an occasion with festivities.

definitions.meaning: swindles or frames someone, a colloquial sense
sews together a tear (a rent in cloth), closing the gap

explanation.surface: A dishonest landlord cuts the payment due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; here it is a tear in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to frame someone unfairly and to mend a tear with needle and thread.

parts.note: affirmative votes, the ones cast in favour of a motion

explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour are affirmative replies, each one a spoken agreement.

clue.text: Activity in which people fall down before opening time

definitions.text: Activity in which people fall down before opening time

parts.words: Activity in which people fall down before opening time
parts.note: the people jump from an aircraft and drop freely before opening their parachutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall down before opening time' suggests drunks or a pub queue; the opening is of a parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: Freefall parachuting involves dropping through the air for a while before the canopy is opened.

parts.note: an invitation to sit down rather than remain standing, not an open, permanent invitation

explanation.walkthrough: A 'standing invitation' is one that is always open; here it is an invitation to stop standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to sit down is literally an invitation not to remain standing.

clue.text: She's very likely to have kids

definitions.text: She's very likely to have kids

parts.words: She's very likely to have kids
parts.note: kids are young goats, and the female of that animal gives birth to them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman bound to start a family, or a childminder; the kids are young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat bears kids, the word for young goats.

parts.note: not dwelling on old times, but the verb meaning reside put into its past tense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Live in the past' is an idiom for nostalgia; here it asks for a word for live in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of a verb meaning reside or live somewhere.

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is made out of the letters of the following words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Steam or water spouts out of volcanic vents, as from a geyser.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is to pour out or emerge, as a gushing spring does.

clue.text: As good and bad employees may be, with enthusiasm

definitions.text: As good and bad employees may be
definitions.meaning: good staff may be enthused and bad staff sacked, both senses of the same word
inspired or stirred up, as in filled with eagerness

explanation.surface: Workers both keen and hopeless face the same fate, eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays both senses at once: a good employee is fired up, a bad one is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dismissed from a job and inspired or stirred with zeal.

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: A double win prompts a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise or extol, a way of celebrating someone.

indicators.note: in speech means the word for prophet is said out loud rather than spelt

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or visionary

explanation.surface: An aged, wrinkled prophet delivers an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere means dried up and withered, the same quality as shrivelled.

clue.text: One with nervous trouble can be really sour

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of playing cards
a tic is an involuntary twitch from nervous trouble

explanation.surface: Someone with a nervous disorder may become very bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means relating to vinegar, which is markedly acidic and sharp tasting.

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Poems by poets are being aired on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for creative output; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works functions or runs, which is what a machine that operates does.

parts.note: not decanting port wine to leave its deposit behind, but clearing silt from a harbour bed

explanation.walkthrough: Port wine is decanted to remove its sediment; here the port is a harbour whose mud is scooped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing mud and silt from the bottom of a harbour or river with a scoop or machine.

clue.text: Part-used transport is exchanged for a better vehicle

definitions.text: Part-used transport is exchanged for a better vehicle

indicators.note: to transport is to move things from place to place, so the letters are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: A secondhand car is part-exchanged for a superior model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trades up swaps an old item for a newer, better one, paying the difference.
